record.paper_title: Completeness of sets of complex exponentials in convex sets: open problems
record.original_question: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity. For X = [-a,a] with a > 0 on the real axis, take H(X) = C[-a,a], and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. Completeness means that the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) equals H(X). What precise condition, preferably expressed through the density of Λ and the geometry of X, characterizes exactly when Exp Λ is complete in C[-a,a]?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
1) X = [-a,a] is a segment on real axis R, a > 0, and H(X) = C[-a,a].

(1-?) No precise condition is known for the completeness of systems Exp Λ in [-a,a], and finding such a condition is a very difficult problem. In this case we present a test for the completeness of systems Exp Λ in [-a,a] to within a single exponential.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda = \{\lambda_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with $0 \notin \Lambda$ and $\lambda_n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$. Let $a > 0$ and consider the segment $X = [-a,a] \subset \mathbb{R}$. Let $C[-a,a]$ denote the Banach space of continuous complex-valued functions on $[-a,a]$ with the uniform norm. The exponential system associated to $\Lambda$ is
$$\operatorname{Exp}\Lambda = \{e^{\lambda_n z} : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subset C[-a,a].$$
We say that $\operatorname{Exp}\Lambda$ is complete in $C[-a,a]$ if the closure of its linear span in $C[-a,a]$ equals $C[-a,a]$.

Problem. Find a precise necessary and sufficient condition, expressed through a suitable notion of density of the sequence $\Lambda$ and the geometry of the segment $[-a,a]$ (in particular its length $2a$), characterizing exactly those sequences $\Lambda$ for which $\operatorname{Exp}\Lambda$ is complete in $C[-a,a]$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of finding an exact density-type criterion for completeness of complex exponential systems on a real segment is a classical long-standing open problem. Known results (Beurling–Malliavin, Levinson, Koosis, Redheffer) give sharp criteria for completeness "up to a finite number of exponentials" or in weighted/Paley–Wiener settings, but no exact characterization of completeness in $C[-a,a]$ is known. Recent surveys continue to list it as open.

status_evidence.title: Completeness of sets of complex exponentials in convex sets: open problems
status_evidence.snippet: No precise condition is known for the completeness of systems Exp Λ in [-a,a], and finding such a condition is a very difficult problem.
status_evidence.claim: The exact completeness criterion on a real segment is stated as an unsolved open problem.
